subject: Re: Kickoff: muNet multitask evolution — April status + task-order risk
body:
Hi both,

Status: Milan finished the port — the muNet evolution loop runs on our stack, and reproduction matches the published notebook results on the benchmark suite. Dynamic task addition works: I introduced retrieval task 3 into a system already trained on tasks 1–2, mu2Net-style, and it reached fork-level quality using 41% fewer added parameters than a full fine-tuning fork.

The risk I want on the record: task-introduction order matters more than the papers emphasize at our scale. Adding the noisy click-feedback task before the clean relevance task degraded the shared components — average quality across all three tasks ended 1.3 points lower than the reverse order. With 11 tasks the ordering space is unsearchable, so the adoption proposal needs either a curriculum heuristic (clean-to-noisy seems to work) or an isolation guarantee for shared parameters.

Hyun suggests borrowing a freeze-then-branch policy from his pruning work; we'll test it next sprint.

Yara
